Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned:

What we covered
- Demoed Redwood hosted inference with streaming and variable context lengths.
- Walked through cost levers: batching, caching, quantization, and context-length pricing implications.
- Reviewed potential fallbacks (32k -> 8k) and RAW token accounting for prompt vs completion.

Your ask
- A simple pricing sketch that maps your expected token volumes and context-length distribution to a target $/1M tokens so you can validate budget.
- Confirmation of whether you’ll need 32k or 128k context for the pilot.

Next steps (proposed)
1) You share rough monthly token volumes split by context-length bucket (8k / 32k / 128k) and avg prompt/completion tokens.
2) We return a unit economics sheet (attachment) showing: $/1M tokens for each profile, estimated monthly spend, and recommended model/quantization profile to hit target unit cost.
3) Quick 30-min follow-up next week to review numbers and lock pilot scope.

To make this easier, below is a short template you can paste into a reply:

- Avg prompt tokens per request
- Avg completion tokens per request
- % of requests that require >8k, >32k, >64k context
- Target budget (monthly) or target $/1M tokens

I attached a one-page pricing sketch and a small sample CSV you can populate.

Thanks, talk soon,

Marissa / Alex,

Thanks for the details — this is great and very actionable. Quick pass below (high-level pricing sketch, attached formal PDF).

Assumptions we used
- Model: open-llama-13b q4f16 baseline for pilot (good latency/cost trade-off).
- Quantization: q4f16 or q8_0 for bulk workloads.
- Blended approach: we present a blended $/1M tokens to the customer for ease, plus optional line items for prompt vs completion in the appendix.

Pricing sketch (blended) — $/1M tokens (hosted, reserved pilot rates)
- 8k context profile: $5.50 / 1M tokens
- 32k context profile: $9.00 / 1M tokens
- 128k context profile: $18.00 / 1M tokens

Why blended?
- Prompt tokens are often cacheable/prefix-heavy; when prefix caching is enabled we effectively reduce billed prompt tokens for repeat prefixes.
- Completion tokens drive steady compute per token — we show both to help tradeoffs.

Estimate for Acme (using their distribution)
- Effective avg tokens per request = 420 + 160 = 580 tokens/request
- Monthly tokens = 580 * 250k = 145M tokens/month
- Weighted context profile cost: (0.71 * $5.50) + (0.22 * $9.00) + (0.06 * $9.00) + (0.01 * $18.00) \u2248 blended $6.45 / 1M tokens
- Estimated monthly cost = 145 * $6.45 \u2248 $9350 / month (falls at low end of their target)

Recommendations to hit target $5-$8 / 1M
- Enable prefix caching aggressively on repeated retrievals (could reduce billed prompt by ~10-25% depending on overlap).
- Use q4f16 quantization for production pilot; move to mixed q8 variant for high-volume tails if latency tolerates small degradation.
- Consider routing 64k+ requests to a higher-cost-capacity but only when needed; otherwise serve truncated context with a follow-up detailed retrieval flow.

Attachments
- redwood_pricing_estimate_q2.pdf (formal sketch with model and tier notes)
- context_length_sample_profile.csv (filled with the numbers you provided)

Next steps
- Marissa: share this with Acme and call out any changes.
- Alex: if this looks good, we can lock pilot terms (reserved pilot with 3-month minimum) and schedule onboarding next week.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the assumptions.

—Rishi
